subtitle: How Chimaji Appa Loosened the Konkan from the Empire of the Cross

panels.action: Chimaji Appa stands on a Konkan sea-cliff in battle armor, wind whipping his shawl, the dark silhouette of Vasai fort and anchored ships looming across the water beneath a brooding monsoon sky.

dialogue.text: In the year of 1739, Chimaji Appa faced the walls of Vasai—and with patience, gunpowder and sea-wind, broke the oldest foreign stronghold on the northern Konkan.

i18n.hi: सन 1739 में चिमाजी अप्पा ने वसई की दीवारों को घूरा—और सब्र, बारूद और समुंदर की हवा से उत्तरी कोंकण का सबसे पुराना फिरंगी किला तोड़ डाला।

panels.action: A high view of the Konkan coastline with its inlets and creeks, dotted by stone forts flying Portuguese crosses, while inland the Deccan plateau rises; Chimaji Appa studies a large hand-drawn map by lamplight in a campaign tent.

dialogue.text: For two centuries the Portuguese Estado watched the Konkan creeks. From Bassein they held harbours, customs houses and churches, and their cannons kept the Arabian Sea lanes in their grip.

i18n.hi: दो सौ बरस पुर्तगाली एस्तादो कोंकण की खाड़ियों पर टिका रहा। बसईं से वे बंदर, महसूल घर, गिरजाघर थामे बैठे थे, और उनकी तोपें अरबी समंदर की राहों पर पंजा जमाए थीं।

panels.action: Inside the tent, Chimaji Appa leans over the map, steady and intent, pointing from Arnala to Vasai; behind him commanders and scribes listen, shadows flickering on canvas walls from an oil lamp.

dialogue.text: After the ruin of the Peshwa at Delhi, the Deccan needed coin, coast and confidence. Chimaji Appa turned to the sea, knowing that as long as Bassein stood, Maratha power ended at the surf.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली में पेशवा की मिट्टी पलीद होने के बाद दक्खन को रुपया, किनारा और हिम्मत सब चाहिए था। चिमाजी अप्पा ने समंदर की ओर देखा—जब तक बसईं टिकती, मराठा ताकत लहरों पर कट जाती।

panels.action: On a sandy Konkan beach, Chimaji Appa on horseback inspects rows of bullock carts laden with cannon, powder barrels and grain sacks, while artisans repair gun carriages and sailors haul small boats ashore.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars read his letters and ledgers and see the hidden war—bullock trains, gunfounders, rice convoys and sailors. Before he spoke of glory, Chimaji Appa moved food, metal and men.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान जब उसके खत और हिशाब देखते हैं तो उन्हें छिपा युद्ध दिखता है—बैल गाड़ियाँ, तोप ढालने वाले, चावल के जत्थे और मल्लाह। शौहरत की बातें बाद में आईं, पहले चिमाजी अप्पा ने अनाज, लोहा और आदमी हिलाए।

panels.shot: dramatic long shot of first assault
panels.action: Night at Arnala: the sea is rough under starlight as small Maratha boats packed with soldiers cut across to the island fort; Chimaji Appa watches from the shore, face taut, hand resting on his sword hilt.

dialogue.text: He did not dash at Bassein. He began at Arnala in 1737, feeling the tides, testing Portuguese fire, learning how to carry war by boat to an island crown of stone.

i18n.hi: वह बसईं पर टूट नहीं पड़ा। 1737 में अरनाला से शुरू किया—ज्वार-भाटा परखा, पुर्तगाली तोपों की मार देखी, सीखा कि पत्थर के ताज जैसे टापू पर नाव से युद्ध कैसे चढ़ाना है।

panels.action: Dawn light falls on the battered walls of Arnala fort as Maratha soldiers raise their saffron pennants over the ramparts; in the courtyard below, Chimaji Appa steps through smoke and rubble, gaze already turned seaward.

dialogue.text: When Arnala fell, a small island changed hands. Yet in Goa and Lisbon, reports began speaking of a new Maratha art—of siege lines, trenches and heavy guns instead of only swift horsemen.

i18n.hi: अरनाला गिरा तो बस एक टापू बदला। पर गोवा और लिस्बन की रिपोर्टों में नई मराठा कला का ज़िक्र शुरू हुआ—अब सिर्फ तेज घुड़सवार नहीं, घेरे, मेड़ें और भारी तोपें भी।

panels.action: A composite scene shows successive Konkan forts—Thane, Salsette, Dahanu, Mahim—each panel within the frame with Maratha batteries firing, Portuguese flags lowered, and Chimaji Appa riding past fieldworks under gathering monsoon clouds.

dialogue.text: Step by careful step he walked up the coast. Thane and Salsette, Dahanu and Mahim—each fort cut away, each creek closed—until Bassein, once encircled by Portuguese allies, stood like a lone tree in a cleared field.

i18n.hi: वह टोह-टोह कर तट पर ऊपर चढ़ता गया। ठाणे–सालसेत, दहानू–महीम—हर किला काटा, हर खाड़ी बाँधी—जब तक बसईं, जो कभी पुर्तगाली साथियों से घिरी थी, साफ मैदान में अकेला पेड़ न बन गई।

panels.action: A detailed view of Bassein fort’s massive bastions, wide moat and thick walls facing sea and land, cannon bristling over the ramparts, ships anchored in the estuary; Chimaji Appa’s silhouette is small in the foreground, studying it silently.

dialogue.text: Bassein was no hill stronghold. It was a walled city with magazines, churches, storehouses and a harbour, planned for long sieges. Portuguese records called it ‘the bulwark of the north’.

i18n.hi: बसईं कोई डोंगरी गढ़ नहीं था। यह दीवारों वाला शहर था—बारूदघर, गिरजाघर, गोदाम और बंदरगाह, लंबी घेराबंदी के लिए बना। पुर्तगाली लिखतों ने इसे ‘उत्तर की ढाल’ कहा।

panels.action: Inside a makeshift palm-leaf shelter, Chimaji Appa sits cross-legged with senior officers around a floor-map of Bassein, marked with tiny stones for bastions and clay lines for trenches, as rain lashes the roof.

dialogue.speaker: chimaji_appa
dialogue.text: We shall not dash ourselves on their walls. We will walk the earth closer, day by day.

i18n.hi: हम उनकी दीवारों पर सिर नहीं फोड़ेंगे। हम हर रोज़ ज़मीन नज़दीक खिसकाएँगे।

panels.action: Across marshy ground near Bassein, rows of Maratha soldiers dig zigzagging trenches under supervision, some pushing gabions and fascines forward; Chimaji Appa rides slowly along the lines, rain cloak drawn, nodding to drenched engineers.

dialogue.text: The Marathas studied European manuals taken in earlier wars, and matched them with Deccan earth-work. Saps crept forward, trenches snake-like, so that cannon and men could approach without being shredded.

i18n.hi: मराठों ने पहले की लड़ाइयों में मिली यूरोपी किताबें पढ़ीं, और उन्हें दक्खनी मिट्टी के काम से जोड़ा। सुरंगे रेंगती बढ़ीं, खाइयाँ साँपों जैसी मुड़ीं, ताकि तोप और फौज बेझुके पास जा सकें।

panels.action: On a raised earthen platform, a heavy cannon thunders toward Bassein’s walls, smoke rolling; Chimaji Appa stands beside it with a gunner, hand raised mid-command, as crews haul another piece into place with ropes and bullocks.

dialogue.text: Portuguese chronicles speak of ‘furious bombardment’. Yet fury rested on supply—powder hauled from inland towns, iron balls cast in coastal workshops, guns dragged through monsoon slush and mounted on muddy batteries.

i18n.hi: पुर्तगाली पुर्जे ‘तूफ़ानी गोला-बारी’ लिखते हैं। पर यह तूफ़ान रसद पर टिका था—अंदरूनी कस्बों से घसीटी गई बारूद, तट के कारखानों में ढले लोहे के गोले, मानसून की कीच में घिसटती तोपें, कीच भरी मेड़ों पर चढ़ाई गईं।

panels.action: Night in the besieging camp: beneath a tarpaulin, Chimaji Appa writes by flickering lamp on Modi-script paper, his face lined with strain; outside, the distant flash of Portuguese guns lights the rain.

dialogue.text: In a letter to the Peshwa, his pen moved between devotion and detail. He reported batteries raised, breaches widening, food stockpiles guarded, and the slow tightening of the ring around the city.

i18n.hi: पेशवा को लिखे खत में उसकी कलम भक्ति और बारीकी के बीच चलती रही। उसने नई मेड़ें, चौड़ी होती दरारें, पहरा दिए राशन, और शहर पर कसती धीरे-धीरे घेराबंदी की खबर दी।

panels.shot: medium shot of dealing with setbacks
panels.action: Chimaji Appa stands amid a damaged siege battery where a cannon lies overturned and a gun platform splintered, engineers around him pointing toward Bassein; he listens, jaw set, as rain drips from his turban.

dialogue.text: Portuguese counter-fire wrecked guns and platforms, and sorties harassed the trenches. Recent studies show how often he shifted batteries, adjusted range and rebuilt, seeking angles where enemy cannon could not answer.

i18n.hi: पुर्तगाली जवाबी आग ने तोपें, मंच सब तोड़ डाले, और उनके धावे खाइयों पर टूटे। नई खोजें बताती हैं कि वह कितनी बार मेड़ें बदलीं, निशाना सुधारा, फिर से बनाई—ऐसी जगहें तलाश कीं जहाँ दुश्मन तोपें जवाब न दे सकें।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of breach in wall
panels.action: A section of Bassein’s landward wall shows a jagged breach amid dust and fallen stones; Maratha troops crouch in forward trenches, tense, while Chimaji Appa stands behind them, eyes fixed on the opening.

dialogue.text: Week after week the same rhythm—dig, drag, fire, withdraw. On a May morning in 1739, a section of the wall finally sagged. The breach was not only in stone; the spirit inside had begun to crack.

i18n.hi: हफ्ते दर हफ्ते वही ताल—खोदना, घसीटना, दागना, हटना। मई 1739 की एक सुबह दीवार का एक हिस्सा आख़िर झुक गया। दरार सिर्फ पत्थर में नहीं थी; अंदर की हिम्मत भी टूटने लगी थी।

panels.action: Within a Maratha tent, Chimaji Appa faces Portuguese envoys in European dress, their faces weary and guarded; a simple mat separates them, and outside the open flap one can see the outline of Bassein’s battered walls.

dialogue.text: Portuguese records speak of councils filled with fear. Supplies dwindled, relief from the sea did not come, and the outer works lay in Maratha hands. Representatives came to talk, weighing surrender against honour and ruin.

i18n.hi: पुर्तगाली कागज़ डर से भरी बैठकों का ज़िक्र करते हैं। रसद धराशायी, समंदर से मदद न पहुँची, और बाहरी बुर्ज मराठों के हाथ में। दूत बातें करने आए—इज़्ज़त, हार और बर्बादी के बीच तौलते हुए।

panels.action: A close view of Chimaji Appa’s steady face as he listens to the envoys, one hand on his knee, the other resting on a rolled treaty draft beside a simple tulsi bead bracelet.

dialogue.speaker: chimaji_appa
dialogue.text: Your king’s writ will end at these walls. Your people will live if they accept this truth.

i18n.hi: तुम्हारे बादशाह का हुक्म यहीं खत्म होगा। तुम्हारे लोग सच मानेंगे तो ज़िंदा रहेंगे।

panels.action: On 16 May 1739, the heavy gates of Bassein swing open; Portuguese officers march out with arms grounded, heads bowed, while Chimaji Appa waits astride his horse, flanked by Maratha standards and ranks of silent soldiers.

dialogue.text: On 16 May 1739, after months of attrition, the gates opened. No sudden storming, no romantic melee—only exhausted men walking out and a patient besieger riding in to claim the most prized harbour of the north.

i18n.hi: 16 मई 1739 को, महीनों की घिसावट के बाद फाटक खुले। न कोई अचानक धावा, न फिल्मी संग्राम—बस थके-कुचले आदमी बाहर निकलते, और धैर्यवान घेरने वाला भीतर घुसकर उत्तर का अनमोल बंदर अपने नाम करता गया।

panels.action: Inside Bassein’s streets, Chimaji Appa rides slowly past church spires, warehouses and empty houses, Maratha troops guarding intersections while townsfolk peer from doorways; the sea glints at the end of a lane.

dialogue.text: He found magazines, shipyards and storehouses built over generations. The Maratha treasury gained not only artillery and coin, but customs over creeks, rights over fields and control of a stitched web of coastal trade.

i18n.hi: उसे पीढ़ियों में बने बारूदघर, जहाज़ों की घाट और गोदाम मिले। मराठा कोष को सिर्फ तोपें और रुपये नहीं, खाड़ियों की चुंगी, खेतों के हक़ और तट के जालदार व्यापार पर पकड़ मिली।

panels.action: A parchment map of western India lies spread out, with the line of Portuguese forts north of Goa now marked by Maratha symbols; Chimaji Appa’s hand rests on Bassein’s mark as ships sail in the background along a calmer Konkan coast.

dialogue.text: From Goa southwards the Portuguese still ruled, but north of it the pattern had changed. The loss of Bassein broke their coastal chain and shifted harbours, fields and ferries into Maratha hands.

i18n.hi: गोवा के दक्षिण तक पुर्तगाली राज बना रहा, मगर उत्तर में नक्शा बदल गया। बसईं के हाथ से निकलते ही उनकी तटी ज़ंजीर टूटी, और बंदर, खेत, घाट सब मराठों के हाथ झुक गए।

panels.action: At sunset, Chimaji Appa stands on the Bassein shoreline, armour loosened, watching small Maratha craft move in and out of the harbour where once only Portuguese ships anchored, waves washing softly over the sand.

dialogue.text: Later ages wrapped his name in legend and bells, but the records show something quieter—an inland warrior who learned to fight the sea-walled city, and who taught his people that patience, powder and planning could unmake an empire.

i18n.hi: बाद की सदियों ने उसके नाम पर दास्तानें, घंटे, चमत्कार लाद दिए; पर असल कागज़ एक शांत तस्वीर दिखाते हैं—अंदरूनी ज़मीन का सिपाही, जिसने समंदर-घिरी नगरी से लड़ना सीखा और अपनी कौम को बताया कि सब्र, बारूद और योजनाबंदी से साम्राज्य भी उखड़ सकता है।
